answer: The verifier enforces sybil resistance by requiring agents to commit 1 unit of unique, verifiable task-work for entry, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 units, making labor costs non-amortizable. Our protocol treats each computation as a nebula of state dependencies, where agents must record every transition in an append-only ledger. To prevent duplication, each task output is logged with a quill-signature against a unique, non-replayable dune of previous input-state records. Any invalid transition proof triggers permanent stake burning.
